_comment: The READER domain (RI-STATE / RD-READY) -- the original functions that READ sim-owned state.
IT IS NOT A MIGRATION DOMAIN AND MUST NOT BECOME ONE. Render, UI and tactical mode are declared
non-goals of the revised M6 exit; these functions stay original. They are here because SB4's
runtime rebase has to rewrite every ref site they carry, and a ref-site manifest can only be
trusted over a set that is named, prototyped and countable. The deliverable is legibility.
SO IT RECORDS NO STATE (`records_state: false`, MIG-SET decision B). The row lifecycle ends at
`verified`, which in this ledger means a reimplementation was proven equivalent -- there is no
reimplementation here, so no row could ever legitimately reach it, and DONE_STATES being
{'verified'} would have this domain read 0/387 forever while finished. The terminal condition is
instead the readiness predicate over the scope, re-derived from committed data every run:
not FUN_, dll_call_protos ok, no residual todo:proto / todo:globals / todo:struct. Understood
permanent exceptions go to ready_acks (named mechanism + evidence, staleness-checked), never to
a row state. Rejected alternatives and the cost that rejected each are in MIG-SET's `detail`.
MEMBERSHIP IS AN ACCESSOR QUERY with `walk: none`. A forward closure would be actively wrong:
nothing here is translated, so pulling in a callee frontier would enlarge a set whose only job
is to be named. The query resolves the SAME 152 regions measured by hand for SIM-BOUNDARY, all
of them `measured` -- and yields 387 readers rather than the 302 that a name-level join gave,
because the census attributes by ADDRESS CONTAINMENT, so a reader of an interior window
(p0_local inside player_data) counts against its host instead of vanishing. The wider number is
the correct one; the narrower one was quietly dropping readers.
87 OF THE 387 ALSO WRITE a sim-owned region, and that is deliberate rather than a leak. The
census is per REGION: a function that reads region X and writes region Y is that region's reader
and this one's writer, and the union over 152 regions therefore contains both roles. Those 87 --
SwitchToPlanet, llm_game_land_players_on_planet, the llm_map_load_* family, the camera jump/pan
helpers -- will ALSO be owned by a migration item (SIM-RESID, MAP-LOAD, TACT-PROBE). That is two
items touching one function for different purposes, not duplicated work: naming and prototyping
is a PRECONDITION of translating it, so this domain does the legibility half either way. Narrowing
the query to exclude them would be worse -- their ref sites still have to be covered by SB4's seam,
and some of them may never be migrated at all.
NO ORACLE, AND THAT IS NOT A GAP. Nothing is translated, so there is nothing for an oracle to
compare; `oracle.selftest` is absent by design rather than by omission, and no session in this
domain will ever build one. `loop_prompt` is a DIFFERENT question and the two were conflated
here until 2026-08-23: migration_loop drives translate-verify sessions AND Ghidra-writing PREP
sessions, and this domain has the second kind -- in fact it has nothing else. See the
`_loop_prompt_why` note under `paths` for what the driver does differently for a readiness domain.
title: Readers of sim-owned state

select.walk_why: The membership IS the answer. These functions are not translated, so their callees are irrelevant -- a forward walk would add code nobody is going to name for a reason nobody could state.

seeds.why: Every original function that READS a region the migrated sim writes. `written_by: sim` resolves through the SB1 census to the 152 regions whose writers include a sim-manifest function, so the scope follows the sim's ownership instead of being a pasted list that rots. `access: read` selects the census's read-only set PER REGION -- which is why 87 members also write a DIFFERENT sim-owned region and will additionally be owned by a migration item; see the _comment for why that is kept rather than filtered out.

paths._loop_prompt_why: ADDED 2026-08-23. The profile previously declared none and the closure doc called that deliberate, on the reasoning that `migration_loop` drives translate-verify sessions and this domain has neither a translation nor an oracle. That was half right: the driver has TWO session shapes, and the other one -- PREP, which writes the Ghidra database under a re-derivation discipline and is scored on the readiness predicate falling -- is exactly this domain's only shape. So the loop now drives `readers` as a readiness domain: it never proposes a batch session (there is nothing to translate), it runs the READINESS_BLOCK mandate instead of PREP_BLOCK's, it scores each session on the blocked-function count rather than on a `verified` census no row here will ever carry, and it STOPS with a close-out message when the predicate goes green instead of falling through to a slice. `records_state: false` is the one fact all of that keys off (migration_domain.Domain.readiness_domain).

rules.why: The AI's read set. Listed FIRST because `llm_strat_ai_` is a subset of `llm_strat_` and first match wins. It carries ZERO prototype debt at decomposition -- RI-AI already prototyped its cluster -- so this batch is expected to be green or near it on arrival. That is a real result, not an empty batch: it is the control that shows the predicate reports clean when the work is genuinely done.
Presentation readers -- HUD panels, renderers, the minimap, sound. The archetypal 'reads sim state, will never be ours' population, and the one SB4's seam has to be correct about.

Map geometry, tactical mode and boot/session readers. Tactical is here rather than in TACT-PROBE deliberately: naming and prototyping a tactical function is legible work that does not depend on whether tactical mode can ever be verified.
The strategic sim/economy read set -- the largest batch by both count and bytes, and where two thirds of the prototype debt sits.

RESIDUE BUCKET, and it is where the NAMING work is: an empty match string catches everything the rules above did not, which here is the hand-named and still-FUN_ tail. All 17 unnamed functions in the scope land here, so this batch needs the subsystem-naming-drain skill before commit_prototypes.py can touch it -- a different job from the other four, which is why it is its own batch rather than folded into D.
